'''Lena Fitting Kourkoutis''' (June 6, 1979 – June 24, 2023) was an American physicist working in the field of [[electron microscopy]],<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20160130010517/https://research.cornell.edu/researchers/lena-f-kourkoutis Lena Kourkoutis] – Cornell Research</ref> and a professor of applied and engineering physics at [[Cornell University]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20190604094859/https://www.aep.cornell.edu/faculty-directory/lena-f-kourkoutis Lena Kourkoutis] – Cornell faculty directory</ref> Her research focused on the use of aberration-corrected [[scanning transmission electron microscope]],<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20160129200227/https://research.cornell.edu/news-features/seeing-more-cryo-stem Seeing More with Cryo-STEM] – Cornell Research</ref><ref>[https://sunspots.cornellsun.com/2017/10/06/office-hours-professor-lena-kourkoutis-discusses-her-research/ OFFICE HOURS | Professor Lena Kourkoutis Discusses Her Research] - Sunspots - Cornell Daily Sun</ref> providing atomic resolution, at cryogenic temperatures (>77K) to study physical processes such as [[superconductivity]]<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1073/pnas.1714901115|title=Nature and evolution of incommensurate charge order in manganites visualized with cryogenic scanning transmission electron microscopy|year=2018 |last1=El Baggari |first1=Ismail |last2=Savitzky |first2=Benjamin H. |last3=Admasu |first3=Alemayehu S. |last4=Kim |first4=Jaewook |last5=Cheong |first5=Sang-Wook |last6=Hovden |first6=Robert |last7=Kourkoutis |first7=Lena F. |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |volume=115 |issue=7 |pages=1445–1450 |pmid=29382750 |pmc=5816166 |arxiv=1708.08871 |bibcode=2018PNAS..115.1445E |doi-access=free }}</ref> and biological structures such as proteins.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lena Kourkoutis: Resolution revolution|url=https://analyticalscience.wiley.com/content/news-do/lena-kourkoutis-resolution-revolution|date=August 6, 2015|publisher=Wiley Analytical Science|access-date=2025-08-05}}</ref>

== Education and career ==

Kourkoutis received her [[Diplom#Germany|Diplom]] in Physics from the [[University of Rostock]], in [[Germany]] in 2003, and conducted her doctoral research at [[Cornell University]], which she completed in 2009.<ref name=MAS>{{cite web|title=In Memory of Lena Kourkoutis, Renowned Electron Microscopist and Mentor|url=https://the-mas.org/2023/06/28/in-memory-of-lena-kourkoutis-renowned-electron-microscopist-and-mentor/|date=June 28, 2023|publisher=Microanalysis Society|access-date=2025-08-05}}</ref> She then moved back to [[Germany]] as a Humboldt Research Fellow at the [[Max Planck Institute]] in [[Martinsried]] between 2011 and 2012, before returning to [[Cornell University]] in 2013, first as a postdoctoral fellow, before joining the faculty.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Dr. Lena F. Kourkoutis (1979–2023): Pioneer and Modern Role Model|first1=Cameron|last1=Varano Casasanta|first2=Bev|last2=Maleeff|date=13 November 2023|doi=10.1093/mictod/qaad084|journal=Microscopy Today|volume=31|issue=6|pages=36–39}}</ref> 

In 2016, Kourkoutis was named as one of the recipients of the [[Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers]].<ref name=OWH>{{cite web|title=President Obama Honors Extraordinary Early-Career Scientists|url=https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the-press-office/2016/02/18/president-obama-honors-extraordinary-early-career-scientists|publisher=[[White House Office of the Press Secretary]]|date=February 18, 2016|access-date=2025-08-05}}</ref>

== Death ==
Kourkoutis died on June 24, 2023, aged 44, after a two-year battle with [[Colorectal cancer|colon cancer]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2023/06/lena-kourkoutis-renowned-electron-microscopy-expert-dies-44|title=Lena Kourkoutis, renowned electron microscopy expert, dies at 44|first=Diane|last=Tessaglia-Hymes|publisher=[[Cornell Chronicle]]|date=June 26, 2023|access-date=2025-08-05}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://hdl.handle.net/1813/113660|title=Lena F. Kourkoutis, June 6, 1979 – June 24, 2023|last1=Muller|first1=David A.|last2=Xu|first2=Chris|date=2023|access-date=2025-08-05}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
* 2023 Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Twelve faculty members elected AAAS fellows|url=https://physics.cornell.edu/news/twelve-faculty-members-elected-aaas-fellows|date=January 31, 2023|publisher=Department of Physics, [[Cornell University]]|access-date=2025-08-05}}</ref>
* 2022 [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2022|title=Fellows nominated in 2022|work=APS Fellows archive|publisher=American Physical Society|access-date=2022-10-19}}</ref>
* 2020 Kurt Heinrich Awards of the Microanalysis Society<ref>{{cite web|title=K. F. J. Heinrich Awards / 2020 Lena Kourkoutis|url=https://the-mas.org/awards/k-f-j-heinrich-award/2020-lena-kourkoutis/|publisher=Microanalysis Society|access-date=2025-08-05}}</ref>
* 2018 Burton Medal from the Microscopy Society of America<ref>{{cite web|url=https://microscopy.org/Society-Awards-Recipients|title=Past Society Awards Recipients|publisher=[[Microscopy Society of America]]|access-date=2025-08-05}}</ref>
* 2016 Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers<ref name=OWH /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://physics.cornell.edu/news/president-obama-awards-early-career-honor-cornell-scientists|title=President Obama Awards Early Career Honor to Cornell Scientists|date=February 21, 2016|publisher=Department of Physics, [[Cornell University]]|access-date=2025-08-05}}</ref>
* 2014 Packard Fellowship for Science and Engineering<ref>{{cite web|title=Lena F. Kourkoutis (1978/79-2023)|url=https://www.packard.org/fellow/kourkoutis-lena/|publisher=The [[David and Lucile Packard Foundation]]|access-date=2025-08-05}}</ref>
* 2013 Albert Crewe Award<ref name=MAS />
